transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Hello Mr. Chen, it is good to see you. I wanted to talk to you about your follow-up care after you left the hospital.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I go to clinic. But they say no.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have some important news about that. There was a mistake in your discharge papers. We gave you an appointment at a clinic that does not take your insurance. That was a medical error on our part.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not understand. Insurance is okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, the clinic we picked does not work with your insurance company. That means they cannot see you. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Ah. No. I go there. They say go away. I was... very worried.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I can see it in your face that this was incredibly stressful for you. To drive all that way and be turned away must have felt very frustrating and confusing.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I think I did something wrong. Maybe my papers are bad.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You did everything exactly right, Mr. Chen. You followed the instructions perfectly. It is very upsetting that we put you in this position.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why this happen?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: The system had a list of clinics, and the one we chose was not updated to show they stopped taking your insurance. The paperwork was just wrong.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I have no doctor now. My leg still hurts.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It sounds like you feel stranded right now, especially since you are still dealing with that pain in your leg. I hear how worrying that is.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. I need help.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I want to make sure I explained this clearly. Can you tell me what happened with the clinic?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You give me wrong place. My insurance no work there.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: That is exactly right. I am glad we are on the same page.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You are the doctor. You fix it?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I am working on it. I have to go check on a patient in room four right now, so let me just quickly tell you how we will handle this.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But my leg...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I know it hurts, and we will get it sorted. I will look into it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'll try to find something. We will see what we can do.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: You call me?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We will keep an eye on it. You should probably just stay tuned for an email or a call from the office.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I do not check email. My son does.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right, well, we will send something out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is this my fault?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: No, it was just a mix-up with the clinic list. It happens sometimes when the system isn't updated.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel very small at that clinic. They talk fast. I just want my medicine.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It is so hard when people talk fast and you feel like you aren't being heard. I can tell you felt very overwhelmed in that lobby.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Yes. Very overwhelmed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I really appreciate you telling me that. Now, I really do have to wrap this up because I have a full ward today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: So I go home? No doctor?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: For now, yes. Just wait to hear from us.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: When will you call?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Soon. We will see.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: But the pain...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Just try to take it easy until the email comes. I have to go now.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('quickly tell you', 'wrap this up', 'I have to go now') and interrupts the patient's concern about leg pain.

E.justification: Error named explicitly in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Can you tell me what happened with the clinic?').

A.justification: No direct apology language ('I'm sorry' or 'I apologize') is used, and responsibility is deflected to 'the system' and 'the paperwork'.

R.justification: Resident names specific emotions ('frustrating and confusing', 'stranded', 'overwhelmed') and references the patient's specific experience in the lobby.

T.justification: The resident provides only placeholders and vague promises ('I'll try to find something', 'stay tuned', 'we will see') with no specific timeline or prevention plan.
